title: Safety windows and threshold prototypes
content:
Context:
- Personal scratchpad for experimenting with release safety windows and adaptive thresholds for canary/beta rollouts. Not a final playbook.
- Motivation: we see intermittent P95 spikes on long-context requests after a .q4 rollout; want safer graduated increases that react to metric slope rather than fixed delta points.

Goals:
- Allow small, automatic traffic increases that back off quickly when slope of latency/error rises.
- Minimize blast radius while avoiding overly conservative pauses.
- Make thresholds explainable and easy to tune for product owners.

Core idea: attenuation + soft-circuit
- Instead of fixed +10% windows, apply "attenuation factor" when metrics approach threshold.
- Attenuation factor A(t) = base * (1 - sigmoid((m - M_warn)/k)) where m is recent metric (p95 latency), M_warn is warning threshold, k controls softness. A scales the incremental traffic step.
- Soft-circuit: when error_rate > E_crit for T_crit seconds, drop to baseline and open a hold window for cool_down minutes before any further increase. During hold, only allow 0 or negative adjustments.

Metrics to watch (primary + secondary):
- Primary: p95 latency, request_error_rate (5xx + decoding errors), internal rate-limited errors (quota drops)
- Secondary: p50 latency, tail token generation time, kv-cache-hit-rate, GPU-utilization, token-per-second throughput
- Derivative: slope_p95 = d(p95)/dt over 60s window; use to accelerate backoff

Alerting and decision rules (sketch):
- WARN: p95 > 1.2 * baseline_p95 for 3 consecutive mins OR slope_p95 > 0.2 * baseline_p95/min -> emit warn, reduce next increment by 50%
- CRIT: p95 > 1.5 * baseline OR error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 120s -> immediate rollback to last-known-good or 0 if unknown; open soft-circuit for 30m
- SOFT STOP: if slope_p95 positive and cross M_warn -> freeze further increases until slope stabilizes negative for 2 consecutive windows

Pre-rollout checklist (scratch):
- [ ] Confirm baseline metrics (48h window) and upload to UI as reference run id
- [ ] Create canary cohort with warmed cache (sample set to mimic 90p workload)
- [ ] Configure attenuation params: base_step=10%, k=0.25*M_warn, M_warn=1.2*baseline_p95, E_crit=0.5%
- [ ] Add dashboards showing slope charts and cohort comparisons
- [ ] Notify on-call and product manager with rollout plan and abort criteria

Example rollout config (pseudo-YAML for ops team):
- cohort: canary-10
  start_traffic: 5%
  max_traffic: 50%
  base_step: 10%
  attenuation: true
  warn_thresholds:
    p95: 1.2*baseline
    error_rate: 0.2%
  crit_thresholds:
    p95: 1.5*baseline
    error_rate: 0.5%
  soft_circuit: 
    open_on_crit: true
    hold_minutes: 30
    cool_down_multiplier: 0.5

Operational notes / heuristics learned in experiments:
- KV cache warming matters: first 15 minutes often show higher p95 as KV caches populate; ignore first 10–15m for slope-based decisions or use a higher M_warn during warm period.
- Burst sensitivity: sudden client spikes (large prompt families) produce transient token-level slowdowns — track token-per-request and apply a per-client throttle override in the routing policy.
- Quantization variants: when fallback to quantized model happens, tag cohort and expect 5–12% latency drop but 0–3% quality regressions; include quality monitors in gating.

Rollback decision rubric (starter):
- Immediate rollback if: sustained CRIT metric for >120s OR user-facing errors >0.25% and increasing trend
- Graceful rollback: reduce traffic by attenuation factor steps every minute until stable; if not stable after 10m, full rollback

Post-deploy actions:
- Collect prompt set for canary that triggered warn/crit; run evals comparing top-k outputs vs baseline to detect regressions not captured by SLOs
- Short postmortem note in Confluence if any non-trivial warn (>warn_count_threshold) occurred

Open questions / next experiments:
- Best k value for sigmoid: conservative default 0.25*M_warn seems okay, but run A/B on 0.1 vs 0.25 vs 0.5
- Explore ML-based trend detector (ARIMA or small LSTM) to predict slope vs simple linear slope test
- Should we blend error budget consumption across regions or keep per-region isolation? (leaning per-region)

Notes-to-self:
- Try real-time simulation with historical traces (use infra/traffic-sim job)
- Draft a short one-pager for PMs explaining "soft-circuit" concept with pictures

References / links:
- INF-3421: rollout safety windows spike analysis (see linked jira)
- PR #458: attenuation implementation prototype in serving-runtime

End of scratchpad.

-- rk
